related_questions.question: What is the current protocol for a positive COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: You should isolate for at least 5 days counting from the day you began feeling sick (Day 0 is the day you began feeling sick; Day 1 is the next day). If you have no symptoms, then isolate for 5 full days after the day you tested positive (Day 0 is the day you took your positive test; Day 1 is the day after).
related_questions.title: What to Do If You Test Positive for COVID-19 - CDPH

related_questions.question: What are the new quarantine requirements for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Updated Guidance: The updated Respiratory Virus Guidance recommends that people stay home and away from others until at least 24 hours after both their symptoms are getting better overall, and they have not had a fever (and are not using fever-reducing medication).
related_questions.title: Respiratory Virus Guidance Update Frequently Asked Questions - CDC

related_questions.question: How long after a positive COVID-19 test do you remain contagious?
related_questions.snippet: While people become less contagious over time, they are still contagious with COVID for an average of eight days. That may vary depending on factors including underlying health conditions and the severity of illness.
related_questions.title: How Long Am I Contagious? - Yale New Haven Hospital

related_questions.question: How many times will I get COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People can be reinfected with SARS-CoV-2 multiple times. Each time a person is infected with SARS-CoV-2, they have a risk of developing Long COVID. Long COVID symptoms and conditions can emerge, persist, resolve, and reemerge over weeks and months.
